10.1002_adma.74086: Alkaline hydrogen evolution (HER) performance of Ru catalysts is limited by the high activation energy barriers of water dissociation and the poisoning of active sites by OH * intermediates. Herein, the Mo x C nanoclusters with distinct crystalline phases (MoC and Mo 2 C) are supported on hierarchical N‐doped carbon nanocages (hNCNC). Long‐range disordered Ru nanoclusters are induced to grow on the MoC nanoclusters due to the presence of Mo vacancies, while crystalline Ru nanoclusters grow on both Mo 2 C nanoclusters and hNCNC due to fewer defects. The Ru‐MoC/hNCNC achieves an ultralow overpotential (@10 mA cm −2 ) of 20 mV, a high turnover frequency of 21.8 H 2 s −1 and robust durability in 1 M KOH, much superior to the counterpart of Ru‐Mo 2 C/hNCNC. The anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis device with Ru‐MoC/hNCNC cathode delivers an industrial‐scale current of 1 A cm −2 at ≈1.65 V in 1.0 M KOH. The theoretical calculation, together with in situ Raman spectra, reveals that the Ru‐MoC heterointerfaces promote the water dissociation kinetics on Mo sites, leading to the detached formation of OH * on MoC and H * on Ru. This spatial decoupling of OH * and H * can mitigate the OH * poisoning of Ru and promote subsequent H 2 formation, thereby demonstrating excellent alkaline HER performance.
10.1016_j.cej.2026.174261: Aqueous zinc-vanadium batteries constitute a highly promising system within the category of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, the low electrical conductivity and the infinite dissolution of V 2 O 5 cathodes in aqueous electrolytes pose significant challenges to the battery system. To address these challenges, a multifunctional interlayer engineering strategy is proposed to enhance the reaction kinetics of V 2 O 5 and enable its stable cycling in AZIBs. The structural and atomic orbital changes in vanadium oxide induced by intercalation agents were investigated using a combination of various spectroscopic and microscopic techniques, complemented by theoretical simulations. Firstly, X-ray absorption fine spectroscopy (XAFS), Mott-Schottky (MS) spectroscopy, Ultraviolet-visible (UV–vis) spectroscopy, and ultraviolet photoelectron (UPS) spectroscopy analyses collectively demonstrate that the intercalation of dodecylamine optimizes the electronic structure of V 2 O 5 . This structural modification facilitates electron transitions to the V 3 d xy state and increases the occupancy of the V t 2g orbitals, thereby enhancing the electrical conductivity of the material. Secondly, dodecylamine has been intercalated into the interlayers of V 2 O 5 to expand the interlayer spacing of V 2 O 5 , thereby ensuring rapid ionic/electron transport. Thirdly, abundant oxygen vacancies generate during the subsequent annealing process, which alleviated the electrostatic interactions between adjacent O atoms and Zn 2+ ions. Fourthly, a flexible graphitic carbon layer derived from the conversion of dodecylamine was encapsulated between the V 2 O 5 layers, effectively alleviating volume expansion throughout the cycling process and further accelerating electron transfer. Leveraging the aforementioned synergistic effect, the as-synthesized electrode demonstrates a high capacity of 403.35 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains a stable capacity retention rate of 92.6% after undergoing 1000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . This work offers novel insights into the structural and orbital changes induced by intercalation and highlights the advantages of intercalated vanadium oxide as a high-performance electrode for Zn storage.
10.1038_s41467-025-67321-3: Bacterial secretion of extracellular polysaccharides is essential for surface colonization, biofilm formation, and pathogenesis. In diderm bacteria, such polymers traverse the periplasm and outer membrane (OM) through outer-membrane polysaccharide export (OPX) proteins that form secretion pores. Among them, Class-3 OPX proteins are the most widespread but lack an OM-spanning pore domain, leaving their mechanisms poorly understood. Here, we characterize WzaB from Myxococcus xanthus as a model for Class-3 OPX-mediated secretion. Structural and molecular dynamics analyses reveal that WzaB exists as a rigid monomer in solution, in contrast to the constitutive octamerization observed in Class-1 OPX proteins. Biochemical, biophysical, and in vivo analyses show that WzaB oligomerizes in a lipidation-dependent manner and directly interacts with the OM porin WzpB and the inner-membrane co-polymerase WzcB, with binding determinants mapped for both partners. Together, these proteins assemble into a trans-envelope polysaccharide secretion complex, redefining OPX function and revealing a distinct translocon architecture for Class-3 OPX systems. Bacteria secrete polysaccharides essential for colonization and infections. Here, the authors reveal the structure and mechanism of WzaB, a Class-3 OPX protein, uncovering a distinct trans-envelope secretion complex driving critical polysaccharide export in diderm bacteria.
10.1109_tpel.2026.3660695: This paper presents a current-driven JK reconfigurable hybrid boost converter that achieves a wide voltage conversion ratio (VCR) range of 7×–30× and delivers 11W output power at 110V / 100mA, targeting electrical stimulator applications. Compared to a conventional boost converter (CBC), the proposed design utilizes series-parallel flying-capacitor (SPFC) stages and a negative-coupled inductor to reduce the inductor current ripple by over 60% and 15% for VCRs ranges of 7×–20× and 20×–30×, respectively. Furthermore, the JK-Controller and current-driven technique dynamically adjust the converter operation based on the stimulus strength setting, leading to a significant reduction in the voltage·ampere (V·A) metric and achieving a stimulation efficiency of 87.3%.
